3) Deletion SLOs & audit evidence — MedNow needs a documented SLO for erasure requests and a sample audit log snippet that shows when a record was marked deleted and when deletion completed.

Hi Silvia — thanks for the detailed list. High level answers below; attaching a short options doc (data-disposition-options.pdf) with examples and risk notes.

Summary recommendations (pilot):
- Retention windows: default "30 days for raw conversational logs + 365 days for structured extracts" with a configurable per-tenant policy. For GDPR-controlled EU data we recommend 30/90/365 but default to 90 days unless customer requests shorter.
- Redaction vs pseudonymization: recommend format-preserving pseudonymization for debugging (deterministic tokens scoped per-tenant) combined with an internal-only reversible vault option (KMS-backed) for escalations. For production-facing transcripts, recommend one-way redaction or masking to minimize re-id risk.
- Deletion SLOs & evidence: we support three standard SLOs — immediate marker (within 1 hour), background purge (scheduled TTL job within 24–72 hours), and final wipe (within 30/90/365-day window depending on chosen policy). We provide a machine-readable audit event per action (example in the attached PDF).
- Field-level erasure: yes, we support selective field erasure. Our pipeline maintains referential integrity by preserving message context metadata while removing or tokenizing specific fields; we also tag dependent fragments and, on request, optionally scrub those parent messages.

Trade-offs in one line: redaction = lowest risk + simpler logs; deterministic pseudonymization = good for debugging and analytics but increases re-identification risk if keys leak; reversible vaulting = highest operational burden and needs KMS/role restrictions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached PDF — it has patterns and an example audit log.
2) If MedNow wants reversible tokens for the pilot, we'll need an explicit KMS binding and an access control list for who can unseal.
3) If you share a field mapping (CSV) we can propose default pseudonymization patterns per field.

I'm available for a quick sync today at 2pm PT or tomorrow morning.

Best,

Subject: Final: Pilot configuration & next steps — MedNow PHI handling

Silvia / Oliver — following up with a concise pilot configuration and next steps. See decisions below and links to the draft playbook.

Agreed pilot configuration (confirmed):
- Retention: conversational logs = 30 days by default; structured clinical extracts = 365 days (configurable). EU tenant data default = 90 days for logs unless MedNow specifies otherwise.
- Tokenization: deterministic tenant-scoped tokens (HMAC-SHA256 with 90-day salt rotation) for debug workflows. Production transcript exports will be masked by default.
- Reversible vaulting: off by default. If MedNow requests reversible unseal, we require a signed KMS policy and approval from MedNow Legal; Redwood will log every unseal event to an immutable audit stream.
- Deletion SLO: marker event within 1 hour; background purge within 24–72 hours; final cryptographic wipe per selected TTL (30/90/365). We will provide an audit event for each stage including event_id, timestamp, actor, and outcome.
- Field-level erasure: supported. Redwood will provide a field-mapping CSV (we populated the template) and a proposed action per field (hash / redact / token).

Action items:
